fullPassage: [1번] When you are successful and the new habit feels normal, it is time to create an anchor. The anchor is valuable for those situations in which you threaten to loose your new habit. I once created the habit of seeing beauty in every human being. So when I felt the habit was mine, I bought myself a geode, a stone that can be found around volcanoes. Geodes are rough on the outside but if you break them in two, inside there is a lovely cave filled with shining crystals. So I put the geode on my desk and after a year or so I had had a row with a person and I was really angry. I came into my office and threw my bag on the ground. "What a bad person!" I said out loud, and immediately my eye was drawn like a magnet to the geode and I realised that here I had a person with a very rough outside, but somewhere inside there must be something beautiful. [2번] Ellen Langer and her colleagues studied the conditions under which people engage in mindless conformity. To forty secretaries at a New York university, they sent a memo that said, "This paper is to be returned immediately to Room 238 through interoffice mail." Like almost all other memos at this university, this one was unsigned. Note that this is a pretty silly request; if the person who sent the memo wanted it, why did he or she send it in the first place? Langer and her colleagues hypothesized that secretaries would go ahead and return the memo without much thinking, because they would follow the norm that says, "Do what memos tell you to do." They were right; 90 percent of the secretaries dutifully returned the memo to Room 238. [3번] Many teachers' analogies are used to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship explained to them, some may understandably visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects. [4번] Few people would dispute that in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Europe and especially Great Britain dominated the world culturally, politically and economically. Britain was the crucible of the Industrial Revolution and its military forces secured the colonies as surely as the English language invaded their cultures. When Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837, she presided over the largest empire in history: the empire on which the sun never set. If you had gone to her court in 1850 and suggested that this empire would be over within a generation, you would have been laughed out of the building. And yet it was true. By the end of World War I in 1918, the empire was fatally wounded and, by the time I was born in 1950, it was a memory.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① valuable=소중한(앵커의 가치 설명 적절), ② ignoring→seeing 오류(모든 인간에게서 아름다움을 '발견'하는 습관이 맞음, ignoring=무시는 반대), ③ rough=거친(geode의 겉모습 묘사 적절), ④ drawn=끌리다(자석처럼 시선이 끌림 적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① valuable: 'The anchor is valuable' — 앵커가 소중하다는 의미로 적절

❌ ④ drawn: 'my eye was drawn like a magnet' — 자석처럼 끌린다는 의미로 적절
det.tip: habit of -ing는 '~하는 습관'. 문맥: '모든 인간에게서 아름다움을 발견' → seeing이 맞음.

❌ ③ colony: '식민지'. 산업혁명의 식민지라는 표현은 역방향 의미
✅ ④ crucible: 도가니/용광로. 산업혁명이 영국에서 치열하게 형성·발전했다는 강렬한 의미. 전체 맥락에서 영국 제국의 힘과 패권을 강조하는 흐름에 가장 적절
det.tip: crucible = 도가니(극한의 조건에서 변화가 일어나는 곳). 산업혁명이 영국에서 탄생하고 발전했다는 의미에 가장 강렬하고 정확한 표현

questions.passage: Few people would dispute that in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Europe and especially Great Britain dominated the world culturally, politically and economically. Britain was the crucible of the Industrial Revolution and its military forces secured the colonies as surely as the English language invaded their cultures. When Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837, she ①<u>presided</u> over the ②<u>largest</u> empire in history: the empire on which the sun never set. If you had gone to her court in 1850 and suggested that this empire would be over within a generation, you ③<u>would have laughed</u> out of the building. And yet it was true. By the end of World War I in 1918, the empire was ④<u>fatally</u> wounded and, by the time I was born in 1950, it was a memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ presided=통치했다(과거동사 정상), ② largest=가장 큰(최상급 정상), ③ would have been laughed→would have laughed 오류(수동태가 맞음), ④ fatally=치명적으로(부사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① presided: 'she presided over the largest empire' — 과거 동사 정상
❌ ② largest: 'the largest empire in history' — the+최상급 정상
✅ ③ would have laughed: 원문은 'you would have been laughed out of the building' — 수동태(have been laughed). 'would have laughed'는 능동태로 의미 변질(비웃음을 당하는 게 아니라 비웃는 주체가 됨)
❌ ④ fatally: 'the empire was fatally wounded' — 부사 정상
det.tip: would have been laughed = 조동사 would + 완료수동(have been p.p.). been 제거 후 능동형 have laughed는 의미 오류

questions.passage: Few people would dispute ①<u>that</u> in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Europe and especially Great Britain dominated the world culturally, politically and economically. Britain was the crucible of the Industrial Revolution and its military forces secured the colonies as surely as the English language invaded their cultures. When Queen Victoria ascended to the throne in 1837, she presided over the largest empire in history: the empire ②<u>on which</u> the sun never set. If you had gone to her court in 1850 and ③<u>suggested</u> that this empire would be over within a generation, you ④<u>would be laughed out of</u> the building. And yet it was true. By the end of World War I in 1918, the empire was fatally wounded and, by the time I was born in 1950, it was a memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ that=접속사(명사절 도입 정상), ② on which=관계대명사 목적격(관계절 정상), ③ suggested=제안했다(가정법 과거완료 병렬 정상), ④ would have been laughed→would be laughed 오류(가정법 과거완료 귀결절은 would have been 필요)
det.analysis:
❌ ① that: 'Few people would dispute that...' — 명사절 접속사 that 정상
❌ ② on which: 'the empire on which the sun never set' — 관계대명사 목적격 정상
❌ ③ suggested: 'If you had gone...and suggested' — 가정법 과거완료 조건절 병렬 정상
✅ ④ would be laughed out of: if절이 had gone(과거완료)이므로 귀결절은 반드시 would have been. would be는 가정법 과거 귀결절로 시제 불일치
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: if + had p.p. → 귀결절 would have p.p. 'If you had gone...you would have been laughed...' — would be는 현재 시제 혼용 오류
